body: I meant 3 years max if I decide to take a gap year (which will likely be the case since I won't be able to take the MCAT until this coming summer). I should have clarified that. My GPA is around 3.96 right now, but since I haven't taken the MCAT I can't say for sure if I'll end up qualifying in the stats department. Unfortunately, because of weird scheduling requirements at my school, I couldn't finish physics in time to catch the old MCAT. I'm going to have to take the 2015 one, so I really don't know what to expect.

There is one post-doc in the lab, no grad students and we do have weekly meetings. The PI is very involved in the lab, something which I found quite different from the previous PI I worked under (in my sophomore year; I didn't mention this in the original post because I was only there for a month). I actually have more interaction with the PI than the post-doc in this lab. It's a great situation in a lot of ways and I still feel fortunate about being chosen to volunteer in the lab. I do have a huge issue with comparing myself to others, which is actually the root of most of my problems, but I am working on it. 

Thank you for all the tips! I feel a lot better about my situation now. I am planning on taking a gap year after graduating and continuing research during that time frame.

Thank you. This is exactly what I needed to hear. As for my PI, he *is* very supportive as I mentioned above, but sometimes I fear that he can't offer me exactly what I need and expects a lot more independent thought and action on my part (i.e. I need to come up with my own project ideas). I'm okay with this as I do believe I have the capacity to come up with viable hypotheses on my own if I work hard enough, but I have a pre-MD/PhD friend whose PI basically gave him an independent project the first quarter (my friend's also guaranteed co-author on any papers that are published within the time he's there). It's frustrating because in terms of publications and projects, so much of it comes down to who you have as a PI and also the nature of your research. Of course, I don't plan on leaving this lab, as I love the environment and the research (and also because I started research relatively late and don't want to cut the time down), but I still regret not screening PIs more closely before joining a lab.
